sentences.text: In a randomized population-based study in Stockholm, 745 healthy individuals underwent colonoscopy with biopsy sampling and 17 of them, 2.3 percent, had colonic spirochetosis.

That study reported colonic spirochetosis was associated with eosinophilic infiltration and a three-fold increased risk for irritable bowel syndrome, with all but one isolate being Brachyspira aalborgi.
The same study reported that the isolates harboured mucin-degrading enzymes and virulence-associated genes, and that standard 16S primers for human microbiota studies failed to detect Brachyspira.
A pooled analysis of 21 studies with individual patient information reported that patients infected with Brachyspira aalborgi were more likely to have lamina propria inflammation.
